analysis.title: SCIB Macro & Markets Chartbook - Political Shifts, Policy Repricing
key_insights: Pablo Hernández de Cos is emerging as frontrunner for the ECB presidency and Klaas Knot may withdraw. Germany nominated Markus Brunnermeier for chief economist. A French candidate is expected to take Schnabel's Executive Board seat. The new president is expected to be named at the 17-18 December EU leaders meeting.
Spanish elections are this Sunday after a final campaign week with televised debates on Monday and Thursday. Forming a new government could take up to 2-3 months.

Marine Le Pen's pension proposal (retirement age 62, or 60 for some long-career workers, plus a funded pillar) claims annual savings of EUR 15-20bn. The 10y OAT-Bund spread tightened 9bp but remains close to recent highs. Santander is cautious about reading too much into the move with the April presidential election six months away.

This week's FOMC minutes were the most hawkish in five years by Bloomberg's index, with 'almost all' participants seeing scope for further hikes. Santander's US chief economist now forecasts one more hike in March 2027, on top of a universally expected hike at the 9 December FOMC.

Markets price one additional Fed hike by September 2027, more than Santander's base case. Santander sees current pricing as overly aggressive and expects scope for a correction toward a less hawkish outlook.

Hawkish US rates repricing pushed EUR/USD below 1.10 for the first time since early 2025. Santander stays structurally bullish on the USD but calls the rally stretched against the EUR. EUR/USD is below the level implied by rate differentials and positioning is already very short, so it advises against chasing the rally.

Santander's ECB financial conditions index is close to its September peak, driven by EUR curve repricing and the equity sell-off. EUR depreciation has only partly offset the tightening. Santander argues the ECB may not need to hike as much as markets price.

Anthropic IPO priced at $83/share for 980mn shares, raising $81.3bn, the largest IPO on record ahead of SpaceX (about $75bn in June). It closed about 17% up on day one and was about 5% above the IPO price pre-market. Fast-track Nasdaq100 entry is expected before year-end at about a 2% weight.

UK CPI rose to 3.6% in October and is expected to keep rising, with the pressure concentrated in energy, airfares and tobacco duty and no sign of second-round effects. US inflation is broader and broadening. Santander argues the BoE does not need to tighten as aggressively as the Fed.

About 19bp of BoE tightening is priced for December. Santander puts the December hike probability slightly below 50%. The market-implied terminal rate is about 4.84% in a year (three hikes), 25bp above the Fed-implied level. Santander's call is one further hike in February with risks of a third later in 2027.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Inflation is concentrated in energy, airfares and tobacco duty, with no sign of second-round effects. This reduces the case for back-to-back BoE hikes.

First time below 1.10 since early 2025, driven by US rates repricing. The move looks stretched relative to rate differentials.

risk_factors: Geopolitical developments and equity market performance are uncertainties for the Fed path.
Renewed Middle East escalation that pushes energy prices materially and sustainably higher could justify a BoE back-to-back hike.
Serious risk of a third BoE hike later in 2027.
Spanish and French political outcomes and French fiscal dynamics.
Anthropic may fail to hold above its IPO price, as several other big IPOs have.
charts_described: Chart 4 plots the Bloomberg hawkish-dovish Fed minutes index, showing the most hawkish minutes in five years.
Chart 4 also compares market and Santander expectations for official rates, with the market pricing one more Fed hike by September 2027 than Santander does.
Chart 5 plots EUR/USD against the EUR-USD 2y spread, with EUR/USD trading below the level implied by the spread.
Chart 7 plots the price performance of the five largest IPOs indexed to 100 at IPO price.
vol_and_positioning: Leveraged funds' net EUR/USD positioning is already very short, which Santander cites as a reason not to chase the USD rally.
Santander's ECB financial conditions index is close to its September peak after the EUR curve repricing and the equity sell-off.
geopolitical: Spanish general election this Sunday, with new government formation potentially taking 2-3 months.
French presidential election scheduled for April, with Le Pen's pension overhaul in focus.
Contest for the ECB presidency and two Executive Board seats.
Possible renewed escalation in the Middle East pushing energy prices higher, cited as a condition for the BoE to hike back-to-back.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish FOMC minutes, resilient US activity and persistent inflation support the market's pricing of an extra hike by September 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Santander sees the pricing as overly aggressive and expects a correction toward a less hawkish outlook, with only one extra hike in March 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Santander cites geopolitical developments and equity market performance as the main uncertainties.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price c.19bp of December tightening and three hikes in total, and December is described as genuinely live.
tension_points.bear_case: Inflation pressure is concentrated in energy with no second-round effects and the labour market is softer, so there is no case for back-to-back hikes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed Middle East escalation that pushes energy prices materially and sustainably higher.

tension_points.bull_case: A resilient US economy, persistent inflation, higher US rates and a wide yield advantage support a structurally stronger USD.
tension_points.bear_case: EUR/USD is below the level implied by rate differentials and EUR/USD positioning is already very short, so the rally looks stretched.

theme_stances.key_argument: Market pricing of an extra Fed hike by September 2027 is too aggressive relative to Santander's March 2027 call.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to see current pricing as overly aggressive
